subject: physics_2
question_text: What are the units and dimensions of disintegration constant?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: from dN/dt = −λN, λ = −(dN/dt)/N. N is a pure count, so λ carries only 1/time. SI unit s⁻¹; dimensional formula M⁰L⁰T⁻¹.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The unit
lines: N is a pure number of nuclei, so λ has the

lines.text: SI unit of λ: s⁻¹ (per second)

steps.margin_note: First mark. λ is a rate per nucleus, so its unit is per second.
steps.why: λ is the chance per second that one nucleus decays, so its unit has to be "per second" — the count of nuclei in the numerator and denominator cancels.
common_mistakes: Writing the unit as seconds. λ is a rate, so it is per second.
Giving becquerel. Bq is the unit of activity A = λN, not of λ.

recall.must_convey: That the SI unit of the disintegration constant is per second, s⁻¹, because λ is (dN/dt) divided by N.
accept: lambda is dN by dt over N
reject: T to the power minus one

steps.memory_tip: λ is a chance per second, so the unit is per second.

steps.label: The dimensions
lines: A number of nuclei has no dimensions, so λ
carries only the dimension of inverse time.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the full formula M⁰L⁰T⁻¹, not just T⁻¹.
steps.why: Mass and length never enter the decay law, so both exponents are zero and only time appears, with exponent −1.
common_mistakes: Adding a mass or length dimension. Neither appears in dN/dt = −λN.

recall.must_convey: That the dimensional formula of the disintegration constant is M⁰L⁰T⁻¹, that is inverse time.
accept: T to the power minus one
M zero L zero T minus one

steps.memory_tip: Only a clock is involved, so only T appears — with a minus one.

insider_note: Derive the unit from λ = −(dN/dt)/N in one line rather than quoting it; the derivation protects the mark if the unit is misremembered.
